newsitem.title: CHINA: China to ban ozone-damaging CFCs from year-end.
newsitem.headline: China to ban ozone-damaging CFCs from year-end.

text.p: China is to ban all aerosol manufacturers from using ozone-damaging chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) in their products from the end of the year, state media said on Saturday.
It was the first time China had banned an industry from using substances harmful to the ozone layer, it said.

Nine central government departments, including the State Bureau of Environmental Protection, the China National Council of Light Industry and the Ministry of Chemical Industry, jointly issued the notice.
The government would not register aerosol products using CFCs after January 1, 1998, and no factories manufacturing such products would receive approval, the notice said.
Factories already established would be dealt with according to the law, the notice said without elaborating.
The ban prohibits government approval for any projects linked to aerosol products containing CFCs, which damage the ozone layer protecting the Earth from the sun's ultraviolet rays.
China had decided to replace CFCs with liquefied petroleum gas and dimethyl ether in the aerosol industry, and to supervise the industry's products that formerly used CFCs, the notice said.
"Enterprises that violate the ban will be punished," the Xinhua news agency quoted one official as saying but gave no details.
